title: Tense scenes in Melbourne as Israel supporters square off against pro-Palestine activists holding 'heartless' vigil three years to the day since the bloody October 7 massacre
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Tense scenes in Melbourne as Israel supporters square off against pro-Palestine activists holding 'heartless' vigil three years to the day since the bloody October 7 massacre

Pro-Palestine vigils were held in Sydney and Melbourne on Wednesday to mark the anniversary of Hamas' attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.

Actual Article Body:
By ASHLEY NICKEL, NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA and NICHOLAS COMINO, POLITICAL REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  20:01 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  21:53 AEST, 7 October 2026

Pro-Palestine protesters have descended on the Melbourne and Sydney CBDs on the third anniversary of Hamas' October 7 attacks on Israel.

The co-ordinated bloody surprise attack on a music festival and the surrounding communities in southern Israel was carried out by the group which controls Gaza.

The terrorists killed about 1,200 people, mostly innocent civilians, which in turn triggered a massive, long-running bombing campaign from Israel on Palestine as retaliation.

Splinter pro-Palestine groups in Australia organised the vigils to coincide with the anniversary in Sydney and Melbourne, while some other pro-Palestine groups were opposed to them being held on the date.

In Melbourne, tensions between demonstrators and police quickly flared as a rival Israeli group held a counter-protest. Pictures from the scene show protesters, notably Israeli activist and broadcaster Avi Yemini, screaming at officers.

The event in Sydney was markedly less chaotic, with a crowd of no more than 150 and speakers reading poetry to the crowd. Though it followed weeks of criticism from politicians, including Premier Chris Minns, who labelled the vigils 'heartless'.

The 'Vigil for Gaza' outside Town Hall, organised by Jews Against the Occupation '48 and supported by a number of pro-Palestine groups, was promoted under the slogan 'Don't Let Israel Steal the Date'.

Promotional material for the event stated that 'its genocidal airstrikes began on October 7th 2023' and called for a vigil to mark the date in solidarity with Gaza.

Pro-Palestine protesters were seen clashing with police in Melbourne on Wednesday, October 7

A large police presence watched over the vigil in Melbourne CBD

The event was held to mark the third anniversary of the October 7 attack Hamas launched on Israel in 2023

The decision to hold the vigil on the anniversary also drew fierce criticism from NSW Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane who weighed in on the issue on Tuesday.

Sloane urged the NSW Government to oppose the event, describing it as insensitive and deliberately provocative.

'It is inappropriate, it is sickening, it is cruel, and it's provocative to be holding these events on October 7,' she said.

'To do it on any other day would show a little bit of credibility. To do it on this day shows their true motivation, which is to provoke, which is to make people feel uneasy, and that is not on.

'At a time when we all need to be coming together and respectfully sharing opinions, this is the antithesis of that.'

Minns was just as scathing and condemned the Sydney vigil, describing the event as 'heartless', while acknowledging authorities had no legal basis to prevent it from proceeding.

'There are some people suggesting it can be stopped. The Constitution doesn't allow that,' Minns said.

'They can certainly do that. It's not against the law, but, as a citizen, I've got a right to make a judgement on it, too.

Organisers claimed the events in Melbourne (above) and Sydney were to highlight the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza

Professional activist Josh Lees was a prominent figure at the Sydney protest

The Sydney vigil (above) was notably quieter than the Melbourne event

NSW Premier Chris Minns had labelled the vigil as 'heartless' given it marked the date of Hamas' massacre of Israeli civilians

Attempts to stop the event in Sydney (above) were found to have no legal basis

'I think these organisers, in many cases, thrive on the notoriety and the attention they get.'

The Sydney event was one of two pro-Palestinian commemorations planned for October 7 in NSW. A separate gathering in Wollongong, organised by Wollongong Friends of Palestine, was advertised as a three-hour event to 'stop and remember the martyrs'.
